passage:
In social studies class, students read about places where rivers were given legal rights. The idea was difficult at first. How could a river have rights?
The teacher explained that such laws try to protect rivers not only as resources for humans, but as living systems. If a river is polluted, people can speak for it in court.
Students debated the idea. Some thought it was strange. Others said humans had not protected nature well enough with old rules.
The class did not reach one answer, but they asked better questions.
The river was no longer only water on a map. It became something with a voice, even if humans had to speak for it.
